description: WCET analysis + schedulability decomposed. Static vs measurement-based WCET, response time analysis (RTA), utilisation bounds, sensitivity analysis, cache behavior on RT, branch prediction effects. The math that proves a real-time system meets deadlines.

sub_mechanisms.name: static_WCET_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: Analyse binary; bound longest path. Considers cache misses, branch prediction, pipeline.
sub_mechanisms.why: Provable upper bound. Tool-based (aiT, RapiTime, Bound-T). Required for DO-178C, ASIL D. Conservative but sound.

sub_mechanisms.name: measurement_based_WCET
sub_mechanisms.definition: Run code with many inputs; observe times; bound worst case.
sub_mechanisms.why: Practical for non-critical RT. Cannot guarantee unobserved paths. Combined with stress testing + safety margin.

sub_mechanisms.name: response_time_analysis_RTA
sub_mechanisms.definition: Iteratively compute worst-case response time per task considering higher-priority interference.
sub_mechanisms.why: Exact schedulability test (vs UB conservative). R_i = C_i + Σ ⌈R_i/T_j⌉ × C_j for higher-priority tasks. Standard RT analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: utilisation_bound_test
sub_mechanisms.definition: U ≤ U_max(n). For RMS: U_max = n(2^(1/n)-1).
sub_mechanisms.why: Quick check; sufficient but not necessary. If passes, schedulable. If fails, run RTA. Cheaper than RTA.

sub_mechanisms.name: blocking_time_priority_inversion
sub_mechanisms.definition: Worst-case time a task waits for lower-priority task holding shared resource.
sub_mechanisms.why: Even with priority inheritance, blocking exists. Added to RTA. Critical path for shared resources. Bounded by longest critical section.

sub_mechanisms.name: cache_effects_on_WCET
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cache hits/misses affect timing. Conservative WCET assumes all misses; tight analysis tracks state.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modern CPUs: huge cache impact. Static analysis tracks cache state at each program point. Cost: complexity.

sub_mechanisms.name: interrupt_blocking_RTA
sub_mechanisms.definition: Interrupts disabled extends WCET. Critical sections add to worst case.
sub_mechanisms.why: RT-friendly code minimises interrupt-disable time. RTAs include this. Bounded by longest critical section in the system.

sub_mechanisms.name: deadline_monotonic_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: DM: priority by deadline. RTA with deadlines that may be < period.
sub_mechanisms.why: Generalises RMS. When deadlines tighter than periods, DM optimal among fixed-priority. Standard analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: EDF_schedulability_test
sub_mechanisms.definition: EDF: schedulable iff U ≤ 1 (for implicit deadlines).
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimal scheduler, simplest test. With deadline < period, density test: Σ C_i/D_i ≤ 1.

sub_mechanisms.name: sensitivity_analysis_slack
sub_mechanisms.definition: How much can WCETs grow before missing deadlines? Slack between actual response time + deadline.
sub_mechanisms.why: Robustness measure. Useful for code changes: 'will adding feature break schedule?' Pre-compute slack; check after change.

sub_mechanisms.name: release_jitter
sub_mechanisms.definition: Variation in task release times. Even periodic tasks may have jitter (clock drift, interrupt latency).
sub_mechanisms.why: Added to interference calculation in RTA. Conservative analysis assumes maximum jitter.

sub_mechanisms.name: task_dependencies_RTA
sub_mechanisms.definition: Tasks may release each other (data flow). Latency = max chain through tasks.
sub_mechanisms.why: End-to-end timing analysis. Single-task RTA insufficient for distributed pipelines. Standard for control loops.

derivation_rules.name: WCET_tight_bound_enables_efficient_schedule
then: schedule reserves more CPU than needed
derivation_rules.why: Conservative WCET → conservative schedulability → wasted CPU. Tight WCET → tight schedule → more workload possible. WCET tool quality matters.

derivation_rules.name: RTA_exact_UB_conservative
if: a task set fails utilisation bound test
then: RTA may still find it schedulable
derivation_rules.why: UB sufficient: if passes, schedulable. UB necessary: only for trivial cases. RTA exact: pass iff schedulable. Use UB for quick check, RTA for tight analysis.

derivation_rules.name: blocking_time_bounded_by_longest_critical_section
then: blocking time ≤ longest critical section using shared resource
derivation_rules.why: Without PI: unbounded blocking. With PI: worst case = one critical section. Schedulability analysis can include + bound. Mars Pathfinder lesson.

derivation_rules.name: cache_aware_WCET_tighter
derivation_rules.why: Naive: assume all cache misses → loose bound. Cache-aware: track hit/miss per access → much tighter. aiT, Bound-T do this. Trade-off: tool complexity.

derivation_rules.name: end_to_end_latency_chains_through_tasks
if: control loop spans sensor → processor → actuator tasks
then: end-to-end latency is sum of per-task response times
derivation_rules.why: Each task contributes. End-to-end matters for control stability. Single-task RT analysis insufficient. Standard for distributed RT systems.
